reports.title: Opera Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results at the Top End of Guidance Ranges

guidance.heading: Business Outlook
section:
Fourth Quarter 2026 Guidance | Full-Year 2026 Guidance
Revenue | $198–205 million | $735–742 million
Year-over-year revenue growth | 12–16 | 20–21
Adjusted EBITDA (1) | $44–47 million | $172–175 million
Adjusted EBITDA margin (2) | 22.6 | 23.5

desk.headline: Revenue up 20% to $182.8m and adjusted EPS up 16% to $0.34; full-year revenue outlook raised to $735–742m

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-IFRS) diluted; IFRS diluted EPS $0.30 vs $0.21

results: Revenue grew 20% to $182.8m, near the top of the company's own range; advertising rose 22% with gaming and travel especially strong, and search revenue rose 17%.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $43.2m (24% margin), above guidance; IFRS profit rose 48% to $27.6m.
Users slipped to 279m a month, but revenue per user rose 22% to $2.60 as growth came from richer Western markets and the Opera GX gaming browser (37m users).
Returned $73.3m in the quarter: $37.7m of share buybacks plus a $0.40 dividend; cash ended at $109.5m with no debt.
Opera will swap its ADSs one-for-one for ordinary shares on Nasdaq from 7 Dec 2026, ending depositary fees.

guidance.summary: Opera raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $735–742m (20–21% growth) and expects adjusted EBITDA of $172–175m. For Q4 it guides to $198–205m of revenue and $44–47m of adjusted EBITDA, a slower 12–16% growth rate as it laps very strong year-end quarters.

points: Management kept some caution in the outlook, citing the wider ad-monetisation environment and EU cross-border rules that slowed e-commerce ad growth.
Gaming ads more than doubled and are now a double-digit share of ad revenue; Q4 spending on new gaming clients and connected-TV inventory is meant to build growth for 2027.
Cost of revenue is expected to jump to about 46% of sales in Q4, trimming near-term margins.
AI remains the product focus: in-browser AI that can act for users, local AI models and connectors for outside AI assistants; MiniPay passed 20m wallets.
PC users reached 100m in October; no formal 2027 guidance was given.
call.source: Call coverage: The Motley Fool call transcript and Investing.com call report, 17 Nov 2026

watch: Q4 delivery against the 12–16% growth range as Opera laps tough year-end comparisons.
Margins as cost of revenue rises with gaming and connected-TV investment.
Trading after the ADS-to-ordinary-share switch on 7 Dec and pace of buybacks.
